findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when a logged-in user opens an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have never visited, tracked, or been emailed about (such as a forwarded email link). The next lines call tu.notification_level and tu.save! without a nil check, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a muted/regular record for that user and topic.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request
findings.body: The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET with only the session cookie for authorization and no CSRF token or signed unsubscribe key. Any third-party page, forum post, email link scanner, or browser prefetcher that causes the victim's browser to request /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe will silently change the victim's notification setting. The mutation is also not idempotent: each repeated visit steps the level down again (watching/tracking to regular on the first visit, then regular to muted on a refresh or second visit), so prefetching, reloading the confirmation page, or revisiting the link produces a different result from the first click and can undo a level the user just re-selected on that page.

findings.title: Unsubscribe bypasses the established TopicUser.change mechanism
findings.body: set_notifications and other notification-level changes go through TopicUser.change, which stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, creates the row if missing, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change so live clients update. This action instead assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls save!, so the change is recorded with a stale reason/timestamp and already-open clients and topic tracking state are never notified of the new level.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires an unsubscribe_url that MessageBuilder does not guarantee
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} into the shared unsubscribe_link string, and both html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder provides defaults for site_name, base_url, and user_preferences_url but not for unsubscribe_url, so any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without also passing the new, undocumented unsubscribe_url (as the previous message_builder spec did) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send the email. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when an unsubscribe_url is present.

findings.title: New unsubscribe behavior has no effective test coverage
findings.body: The only spec change adds unsubscribe_url to the MessageBuilder fixture but the example still only asserts that the user preferences URL appears in the body; it never asserts the per-topic unsubscribe URL is rendered in either the text or HTML part. There are also no specs for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering the watching/tracking-to-regular and regular-to-muted transitions, the slug redirect, or the missing-TopicUser case, so the endpoint's core behavior can regress (or crash) without a failing test.
